One major reason for this is the heterogeneity of the disease and the current lack of operationalized means to distinguish various disease endotypes (molecular subtypes). Biomarkers measured in blood or urine, reflecting joint tissue turnover, have been developed and tested during the last decades. In this narrative review, we provide highlights on biomarkers derived from the two most studied and abundant cartilage proteins – type II collagen and aggrecan. Recent findings Multiple biomarkers assessing type II collagen degradation and formation, and aggrecan turnover have been developed. Several markers, such as uCTX-II, have been validated for their association with disease severity and prognosis, as well as pharmacodynamically used to describe the mode of action and efficacy of drugs in development. There is a great need for biomarkers for subdividing patients (i.e., endotyping) and recent scientific advances have not yet come closer to achieving this goal. Summary There is strong support for using biomarkers for understanding OA, reflecting degradation and formation of the joint tissues, focused on type II collagen and aggrecan. There is still a lack of in vitro diagnostics, in all contexts of use. Keywords aggrecan biomarker osteoarthritis type II collagen OPEN-ACCESS TRUE INTRODUCTION The most prevalent form of arthritis is osteoarthritis (OA). It is associated with overuse of the joints, injury, metabolic and inflammatory factors, and accounts for more than 10% of disabilities and symptomatic diseases of the elderly population [ 1 , 2 ]. Joint pain and progressive degeneration of articular cartilage are hallmarks of the disease which include remodeling of all joint tissues (bone, synovium, ligaments) resulting in painful articular cartilage loss, manifested as radiographic joint space narrowing (JSN) [ 3 ]. Research indicates that the structural integrity and preservation of articular cartilage is highly reliant on normal subchondral bone turnover, synovial crosstalk, physiological biomechanical stresses and intact chondrocyte function [ 4 ]. Both in the clinical and research settings, and possibly most importantly in drug development, there is a need for validated diagnostic tools for treatment selection. Thus, developing markers with these properties is a top priority for researchers in the biomarker field for future management of OA. Disease-modifying OA drugs (DMOADs), i.e., drugs that could ease pain and slow the destruction of joints, have not yet been approved for OA [ 5 , 6 ]. The lack of biological understanding what drives OA and a heterogeneous patient population may explain why no medication has thus far been developed. Therefore, we need to expand our understanding of the subclinical or molecular subtypes, i.e., endotypes, as well as the corresponding markers that allow separation of patient groups. Although many aspects of biomarker development need attention, we have elected to focus on the following: (1) Pharmacodynamic biomarkers allowing the monitoring of treatment responses within a clinical study enabling informed decision making in clinical studies faster and with fewer patients, analogous to the response of HbA1c in type II diabetes studies. (2) Biomarkers reflecting disease activity, which may possibly be used for identification of fast progressors and those in most need of treatment. This will also allow for selection of the optimal patients for clinical studies. Blood, synovial fluid, or urine-based biochemical markers may be used as noninvasive and objective measures to diagnose patients. In these settings, there are a range of confounding factors associated with noninvasive biochemical markers which need to be discussed and considered, to provide the right context for evaluating the potential value of biomarkers [ 7 ]. This narrative review sets out to review current and potential biomarkers for use in OA with focus on cartilage-derived type II collagen and aggrecan markers. We have searched PubMed for recent papers and selected a few to highlight as examples of the research conducted to develop and test biomarkers for OA. OSTEOARTHRITIS – THE STORY IS EVOLVING A long list of biomarkers has been tested in OA for different purposes and listed in several recent reviews [ 7 – 9 ]. For the purpose of a concise description, we will only describe type II collagen and aggrecan, which are the main components of cartilage although other proteins may be of equal interest. Type II collagen – keeping it together Type II collagen is the most abundant protein in cartilage [ 10 ]. It is a fibrillar collagen that acts as the structural framework of the cartilage extracellular matrix (ECM). Collagen attracts attention as its turnover is directly associated with cartilage homeostasis and joint health. Several markers have been developed targeting different soluble metabolites and posttranslational modifications of type II collagen (Fig. 1 ). Formation of type II collagen As the collagen matures both the N- and C-terminal propeptides are cleaved off (Fig. 1 ). Alternative splicing of the first three exons results in two types of the noncollagenous N-terminal pro-peptide—types IIA and IIB. Type IIA is the embryonic variant in which the cysteine-rich region, exon 2, is retained, whereas type IIB is the variant present in mature articular cartilage [ 11 ]. Markers that measure either of the two splice variants have been developed. The PIIANP assay targets the A form of the splice variant [ 12 ]. In the OA biomarker project, Foudation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH, US) study, baseline serum levels of PIIANP were found to be negatively associated with two-year radiographic progression when assessed in 600 OA patients [ 13 ]. An immuno-assay specific for PIIBNP was recently developed [ 14 , 15 ]. The PRO-C2 assay, targeting an epitope at the junction site of exons 1 and 3, only measures released PIIBNP. Compared with healthy controls ( n = 22), PRO-C2 and PIIANP in serum samples were lower in knee OA patients with a KL grade of 2–4 ( n = 123) [ 15 ]. Assessed two independent knee OA cohorts of 106 and 147 participants, Luo et al. reported that low serum levels of PRO-C2 were associated with 3.4-fold higher likelihood of radiographic progression than those with high levels of PRO-C2 [ 16 ▪ ]. This suggests that low cartilage repair capacity, assessed by markers such as PRO-C2 and PIIANP, is a risk factor for OA. The idea of low cartilage formation being associated with OA severity and progression was already proposed two decades ago by Garnero et al. , who showed that the ratio between type II collagen synthesis measured by PIIANP and degradation measured by uCTX-II was altered in OA [ 17 ]. Moreover, these data are now appreciated as indications of different endotypes in OA. PIICP has also been suggested to be a marker of cartilage formation, however to date, it has mainly been assessed in preclinical settings and posttraumatic injury cohorts.

extracted_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates current and potential blood and urine biomarkers for osteoarthritis (OA), focusing on markers derived from type II collagen and aggrecan to reflect joint tissue turnover. The review details their molecular targets, measurement methods, and diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic utility in assessing cartilage degradation, bone turnover, and disease progression, including responses to treatments. It highlights both established and preclinical markers, emphasizing the complexities of cleavage sites, the need for multi-protease inhibition strategies, and further biomarker validation, while noting a continued lack of operationalized in vitro diagnostics and markers for patient endotyping.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Osteoarthritis (OA) biomarker investigation, Doxycycline treatment, Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT), Cathepsin K inhibition, Collagen hydrolysate supplementation, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced remodeling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic dose or intervention protocols are primarily reported, as this is a narrative review focusing on biomarkers for Osteoarthritis and their utility in drug development and patient management. However, some treatments were mentioned: Doxycycline was investigated in a randomized controlled trial in 120 obese knee OA patients (specific dose/duration not detailed). Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) was examined for its effect on knee OA patients (specific dose not detailed). Cathepsin K inhibition reduced CTX-I by more than 90% (specific inhibitor dose/duration not reported). Collagen hydrolysate administration led to a modest decrease in CS846 and an elevation in PIIANP (specific dose/duration not reported). No dose-response comparisons were generally reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher; associated with disease severity and prognosis
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Validated for association with disease severity and prognosis; higher in OA patients than healthy controls, increasing with disease progression and severity. Baseline levels predicted symptomatic and radiographic knee OA progression. Its ratio with PIIANP is altered in OA. Diagnostic value varies by sex and ethnicity. Changes correlated with treatment-mediated disease status changes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A well-described biomarker reflecting the degradation of type II collagen, a key structural component of cartilage extracellular matrix.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Osteoarthritis disease activity and progression, pharmacodynamic studies in drug development, DMOAD trials, oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with OA disease severity and prognosis; can describe the mode of action and efficacy of drugs in development. Distinguishes OA patients, healthy controls, and disease progression rates, predicting symptomatic and radiographic knee OA progression. Its diagnostic value is influenced by demographic variables such as sex and race, and it correlates with treatment-mediated changes in disease status.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Type II collagen formation (synthesis) marker (embryonic variant, type IIA splice variant), protein level.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in OA patients, negatively associated with radiographic progression; elevated in response to collagen hydrolysate.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline serum levels negatively associated with two-year radiographic progression in 600 OA patients. Levels were lower in knee OA patients (KL grade 2–4, n=123) compared with healthy controls (n=22). Elevated after collagen hydrolysate administration, but no specific quantification provided.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the synthesis and formation of type II collagen, a process crucial for cartilage homeostasis and repair.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Osteoarthritis progression, diagnosis, assessment of cartilage repair capacity, response to collagen hydrolysate.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Low cartilage repair capacity, assessed by PIIANP, is a risk factor for OA and is negatively associated with radiographic progression. Its elevation with collagen hydrolysate suggests its role in indicating type II collagen formation.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Type II collagen formation (synthesis) marker (mature articular cartilage variant, PIIBNP)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in OA patients; low levels associated with higher likelihood of progression. In explants, initial decrease followed by increase.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in knee OA patients (KL grade 2–4, n=123) compared with healthy controls (n=22). Low serum levels were associated with 3.4-fold higher likelihood of radiographic progression than those with high levels in two independent cohorts (106 and 147 participants). In explant culture, it showed an initial decrease over three weeks, then an increase over seven weeks during FGF-18 induced remodeling.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the synthesis and formation of mature articular type II collagen, essential for maintaining the structural integrity and for dynamic anabolic restructuring of cartilage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Osteoarthritis progression, diagnosis, assessment of cartilage repair capacity, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced biphasic remodeling process in OA cartilage explants.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Low cartilage repair capacity, assessed by PRO-C2, is a risk factor for OA; associated with a higher likelihood of radiographic progression. It also indicates type II collagen formation during dynamic anabolic restructuring of cartilage.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Suggested to be a marker of cartilage formation

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not specified in relation to Osteoarthritis.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No quantitative data reported; mainly assessed in preclinical settings and posttraumatic injury cohorts.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggested to be a marker of cartilage formation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels in OA cartilage compared to healthy samples.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: ELISA targeting a type II collagen-specific epitope

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 9/10 OA patients vs. 2/10 healthy controls; increased levels associated with increased Joint Space Narrowing (JSN).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Targets a type II collagen-specific epitope upstream of the 3/4 cleavage sites, mainly mediated by MMP-13 activity, reflecting type II collagen degradation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Distinguishes between OA patients and healthy controls, as well as between symptomatic and asymptomatic radiographic OA patients. Increased levels are associated with increased joint space narrowing.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Quantification of elongated C1,2C target sequence.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Urinary C2C was significantly higher in progressors compared to nonprogressors after a 3-year follow-up. Only urinary C2C (C2C-HUSA), but not serum C2C, was associated with knee OA progression.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Quantifies an elongated version of the C1,2C target sequence, specific toward type II collagen, indicating type II collagen degradation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Urinary C2C is associated with radiographic OA progression and is higher in progressors, while serum C2C is not associated.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Measurement of neo-epitope containing a nitration-susceptible tyrosine residue.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels were correlated to subscores of Whole-Organ Magnetic Resonance Imaging Score (WORMS), articular cartilage integrity, and osteophyte scores.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cartilage degradation marker targeting an epitope in the N-terminal triple helical region of the 3/4 fragment of type II collagen.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlates with WORMS subscores and other indicators of articular cartilage integrity and osteophyte formation.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Not specified (derived from Coll2-1, likely urine).
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Measurement of nitrated posttranslational species of Coll2-1.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Independently associated with radiographic OA severity (in multivariate analysis with other markers).

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis, oxidative and inflammatory stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides specificity for molecular pathways in OA and rheumatoid arthritis. Associated with radiographic OA severity.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates radiographic knee OA, but is more significantly elevated and potentially more relevant in rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosis spondylitis.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Measurement of neoepitope generated by MMP-13 cleavage of type II collagen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased in severe OA; decreased with sCT treatment.
